title: Translanguaging in EFAL Assessment: Pre-service Teachers Navigating a “Pedagogy of Compromise"
text_snippet: Translanguaging in EFAL Assessment: Pre-service Teachers Navigating a “Pedagogy of Compromise" In South African multilingual classrooms, assessment remains constrained by monolingual English frameworks, creating a systemic contradiction with additive bilingualism policies. This qualitative study explores how pre-service teachers navigate this contradiction and argues that they are often socialized into a “pedagogy of compromise.” Within this approach, translanguaging is accepted as a scaffold in formative assessment but largely excluded from high-stakes summative assessment, thereby sustaining English's dominance. Drawing on questionnaire and interview data from twenty-fourth-year pre-service teachers, the study, using reflexive thematic analysis, identifies a persistent gap between beliefs and practices. While participants recognized the potential value of translanguaging, many showed conceptual confusion between translanguaging and code-switching. In practice, home languages were predominantly used as a bridge to support learning, rather than as legitimate resources for demonstrating knowledge in assessment. title: Analysis of Ideology and Power in Biden’s Speech at The G20 Summit: A Critical Discourse Analysis
text_snippet: Analysis of Ideology and Power in Biden’s Speech at The G20 Summit: A Critical Discourse Analysis Political speeches delivered at international forums play a significant role in shaping global perspectives, legitimizing policies, and constructing power relations. One of the global economic forums, the G20, provides a strategic platform for world leaders to articulate ideological positions and assert leadership. This study aims to analyze how ideology and power are represented through language in Biden’s 2024 speech at the G20 Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Employing a descriptive qualitative research design, this study uses Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) based on Fairclough’s three-dimensional framework. The data consist of the transcript of Biden’s speech obtained from the official White House website. The researcher analyzed the data systematically by first categorizing Biden’s speech script according to Fairclough’s framework: textual analysis, discourse practice, and sociocultural practice. Each category was then divided into sections based on specific criteria, such as pronoun usage, evaluative lexical choices, and statements related to political or global issues. title: Politeness Strategies in Classroom Discourse: A Study of Teacher-Student Interactions in East Nusa Tenggara
text_snippet: Politeness Strategies in Classroom Discourse: A Study of Teacher-Student Interactions in East Nusa Tenggara This study investigates politeness strategies in classroom discourse by examining teacher-student interactions in two Grade 8 classrooms in two secondary schools in Timor Tengah Utara (TTU) Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. Responding to the need for locally grounded classroom pragmatics, the study combines Brown and Levinson's politeness framework with discourse-analytic attention to sequential context, institutional roles, and cultural expectations. Data were collected over two weeks from two teachers and 42 students through classroom observations, two recorded classroom sessions, field notes, and verbatim transcription. The analysis identified positive politeness, negative politeness, bald on-record, and off-record strategies in teacher and student talk. Teachers most often used positive politeness to invite participation and build classroom rapport, whereas students most often used negative politeness to show respect and manage the asymmetrical teacher-student relationship. Bald-on-record strategies appeared mainly in teacher directives for classroom management, whereas off-record strategies were used less frequently to soften criticism or disagreement. title: A Student Perceptions On The Academic Writing Skills Of English Education Students At Kalimantan Timur
text_snippet: A Student Perceptions On The Academic Writing Skills Of English Education Students At Kalimantan Timur This study aims to investigate how English Education students at Universitas Muhammadiyah Kalimantan Timur perceive their academic writing abilities, specifically regarding the use of ChatGPT and other artificial intelligence tools. At a time when AI is becoming increasingly integrated into education, the study addresses concerns about how these technologies affect writing skills in underdeveloped areas, potentially impacting creativity, motivation, and moral behavior. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the study combined semi-structured qualitative interviews with six purposively selected participants, which were subjected to thematic analysis, with quantitative surveys using a 21-item Likert-scale questionnaire administered to 31 students and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Quantitative results showed generally favorable opinions (mean score of 2.25), with significant suspicion about plagiarism detection but considerable agreement about AI's contribution to efficiency and brainstorming. Qualitative findings emphasized AI as a scaffold and a source of cognitive assistance, tempered by concerns about over-reliance and self-confidence. The findings sugg

title: Local Languages and Global English: English Literature Students’ Perceptions of Linguistic Capital
text_snippet: Local Languages and Global English: English Literature Students’ Perceptions of Linguistic Capital The global expansion of English has intensified debates about the relative positioning of global and local languages in multilingual higher education. While previous studies have examined language policy and English-medium instruction, fewer empirical studies investigate how students simultaneously evaluate local and global languages across multiple dimensions of linguistic capital. This study explores English Literature students’ perceptions of local languages and English in terms of status (prestige), instrumental value (academic–career utility), and identity (affection). Using a quantitative descriptive–comparative design, data were collected from 68 second-semester undergraduate students at an Indonesian university through a structured questionnaire with parallel item sets for local languages and English. Descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and effect size analyses were employed to examine comparative evaluations. The findings show that local languages retain moderate symbolic and identity-related relevance among students. title: Exploring the Integrated Listening-Writing Instruction
text_snippet: Exploring the Integrated Listening-Writing Instruction The study aims to investigate the correlation between listening techniques and students' writing proficiency. The study employed a qualitative technique, utilizing an open-ended questionnaire to gather data from third-semester students in the Indonesian Language and Literature Education Study Program. The findings indicate that students generally employ a blend of traditional and digital listening techniques, favoring versatile platforms like YouTube. The principal findings of the study demonstrate that listening activities serve as catalysts for idea generation and linguistic enhancement in the writing process. This interaction is indirect and contingent upon the students' capacity to transform information into organized writing. The primary challenges in this context include difficulty with idea development, difficulty sustaining concentration, and limited references. This study underscores the necessity of more targeted integration of listening and writing activities in education and enhances understanding of the significance of listening as a component of the strategy for cultivating students' writing abilities.

title: Leveraging AI in Translation Tasks to Improve EFL Learners’ Vocabulary and Accuracy
text_snippet: Leveraging AI in Translation Tasks to Improve EFL Learners’ Vocabulary and Accuracy This study looks into how well AI-assisted translation activities help Indonesian EFL learners improve their vocabulary acquisition and linguistic accuracy. 34 third-semester English Education students at Universitas Muhammadiyah Kalimantan Timur participated in the study, which used a mixed-methods research methodology. A pre-test and post-test translation task that assessed students' vocabulary use and translation accuracy using an equivalency-based assessment criteria was used to gather quantitative data. Semi-structured interviews were used to gather qualitative data in order to investigate learners' opinions and experiences using AI-assisted translation systems. The quantitative results showed a statistically significant improvement in students' post-test scores when compared to their pre-test results, suggesting that learners' vocabulary knowledge and translation accuracy were positively impacted by AI-assisted translation activities. The findings of the paired-sample t-test verified that the improvement was not the result of chance. title: Barriers to Critical Inquiry of Abstract Concepts through Contextual Teaching and Deep Learning in Junior High Schools
text_snippet: Barriers to Critical Inquiry of Abstract Concepts through Contextual Teaching and Deep Learning in Junior High Schools This study investigates the barriers that hinder students at SMP Negeri 1 Gunungsitoli Utara from conducting inquiry into abstract concepts through Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) supported by deep learning strategies. The ability to conduct critical inquiry is essential for developing higher-order thinking skills; however, early adolescents often struggle to analyze and interpret abstract ideas without adequate context and cognitive support. This study aims to identify the cognitive, pedagogical, and contextual factors that constrain students’ engagement in inquiry-based learning activities. A qualitative descriptive research design was employed, involving 38 eighth-grade students. Data were collected through classroom observations, learning assignments, and semi-structured interviews. Data validity was ensured through triangulation, member checking, and prolonged engagement to obtain consistent and credible findings. The findings reveal that students’ difficulties stem not only from limited abstract reasoning but also from the interaction between surface learning habits formed by rote-oriented instruction and insufficient scaffolding during contextual learning. title: Recalibrating Digital Self-Efficacy in South African Higher Education through Structured Digital Literacy Interventions
text_snippet: Recalibrating Digital Self-Efficacy in South African Higher Education through Structured Digital Literacy Interventions Digital literacy has become a foundational requirement for participation in contemporary higher education, particularly as teaching, assessment, and scholarly engagement are increasingly mediated through digital platforms. Despite widespread institutional investment in digital literacy workshops, intervention effectiveness is often assessed through behavioural adoption measures or assumed increases in student confidence. Limited attention has been given to how structured digital literacy initiatives reshape students’ internal perceptions of competence. This study investigates whether digital literacy interventions recalibrate digital self-efficacy within a South African private higher education context. Grounded in an integrated framework that combines Technology Acceptance Model, self-efficacy theory, and Academic Literacies scholarship, the study adopts a quantitative cross-sectional design. Survey data were collected from 428 students, and paired analyses were conducted on respondents who completed both baseline and post-intervention confidence measures. Descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and linear regression analyses were employed to examine changes in self-report

title: Implementation Of Traditional Games In The Learning Of Physical Education For Elementary School Students
text_snippet: Implementation Of Traditional Games In The Learning Of Physical Education For Elementary School Students Physical Education instruction in elementary schools often faces challenges, including low student engagement and limited use of contextual learning approaches. This study aims to analyze the implementation of traditional games in Physical Education (PE) learning at SD Muhammadiyah Ambarketawang 02 and identify the supporting and inhibiting factors influencing its application. This study employed a qualitative case study approach. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed using data reduction, categorization, data display, and conclusion-drawing techniques. The findings indicate that traditional games such as gobak sodor, engklek, long clogs, and tug-of-war were systematically integrated into PE learning activities. Based on observations and participants’ responses, implementing traditional games led to more active, participatory learning situations and encouraged cooperation, social interaction, and student involvement during learning activities. The study also found that traditional games contributed to contextual and culturally relevant learning experiences in elementary schools.

title: Development of SobatAI: A Companion Chatbot for English Language Learning Based on Users’ Passion and Profession
text_snippet: Development of SobatAI: A Companion Chatbot for English Language Learning Based on Users’ Passion and Profession The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into educational practices has enabled the development of adaptive learning tools that provide personalized language-learning experiences. This study aims to develop SobatAI, an English learning companion chatbot that adapts to users’ passions and professional backgrounds. Employing the Design and Development Research (DDR) method, this study consists of three phases: analysis of user needs, system design and development, and usability testing. A total of 75 university students and early-career professionals participated in prototype testing. Findings show that SobatAI successfully provides personalized vocabulary, situational dialogues, and micro-learning content tailored to users’ specific fields, such as technology, health, tourism, and creative industries. Usability scores indicate that the system achieves high acceptance, with an average SUS score of 83.2. The study concludes that integrating personal interests and professional context significantly enhances engagement and relevance in English language learning. title: Literature Study of Microlearning Infusion in English Language Learning
text_snippet: Literature Study of Microlearning Infusion in English Language Learning Microlearning has gained increasing attention as a flexible, technology-enhanced instructional approach in English Language Learning (ELL). However, research on how it is integrated into ELL and its effects on learners remains limited. This study aims to investigate (1) how microlearning is infused into ELL, and (2) how it impacts student engagement, motivation, and learning outcomes. Employing a qualitative descriptive design, data were collected through semi- structured interviews with five university students who had experienced microlearning activities. An interview guide with open-ended questions served as the research instrument, and data were analyzed thematically using coding to identify recurring patterns and themes. The study concludes that microlearning offers an effective learner-centered approach in ELL, especially when incorporated into a blended learning framework. Its implications suggest that educators should strategically design microlearning activities that align with learning goals and provide institutional support to overcome implementation barriers.

title: Culture-Specific Items in EFL Students’ Translation: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: Culture-Specific Items in EFL Students’ Translation: A Systematic Review This study examines how culture-specific items (CSIs) are translated in EFL contexts through a systematic literature review. Using a PRISMA-based approach, this review analyzed 30 empirical studies published between 2020 and 2025. The studies were identified through structured searches in Scopus, Crossref, Dimensions, and Google Scholar. The selection process involved duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and final inclusion based on predefined criteria. Data were extracted by focusing on study design, participant characteristics, CSI classifications, translation strategies, and factors influencing students’ translation performance. The findings show that CSIs are conceptualized through varied frameworks, including realia, culturemes, cultural references, and culture-bound expressions. In practice, their translation relies on flexible strategies such as retention, adaptation, explicitation, and cultural substitution. However, EFL students often face difficulty in selecting appropriate strategies, especially when translating culturally distant expressions. title: Graduate Employability and Perceived Preparedness of PGCE Alumni: A Tracer Study of a Public University in South Africa
text_snippet: Graduate Employability and Perceived Preparedness of PGCE Alumni: A Tracer Study of a Public University in South Africa This study examined graduate employability and perceived professional preparedness (self-reported readiness rather than demonstrated competence) among graduates from a Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE) program at a public university in South Africa. Using a tracer study design, data were collected from 74 graduates via a structured questionnaire measuring employment outcomes, perceived teaching preparedness, and curriculum relevance. Descriptive statistics, nonparametric group comparisons, correlation analyses, and thematic analysis were used. Results showed that only 20.3% of graduates were employed at the time of the survey, although most employed graduates secured positions within six months. Despite low employment rates, graduates reported high perceived preparedness across all assessed teaching competencies (M = 4.63, SD = 0.74), with classroom teaching and lesson planning rated highest. No significant differences in preparedness were found between employed and unemployed graduates. title: Bibliometric Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Research Trends in Writing Skill Development: A Study Using VOSviewer Visualization
text_snippet: Bibliometric Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Research Trends in Writing Skill Development: A Study Using VOSviewer Visualization This study investigates the research trends and thematic structures of scholarly publications on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in writing skill development within the field of English Language Education. Using a bibliometric approach, 312 publications indexed in Google Scholar between 2019 and 2024 were analyzed using VOSviewer. The analysis focused on keyword co-occurrence, density, and temporal evolution to identify the intellectual landscape of AI-related writing research. The findings reveal a significant increase in studies on AI applications in writing instruction, particularly since 2022. The density visualization highlights “artificial intelligence,” “writing,” “machine learning,” and “ChatGPT” as dominant keywords, reflecting the growing intersection between educational technology and writing pedagogy. The overlay visualization shows a chronological shift from early research on automated assessment (2019–2021) toward pedagogical applications and generative AI tools (2023–2024). title: An Analysis Of Phonological Interference Of First Language Towards Student’s Pronunciation
text_snippet: An Analysis Of Phonological Interference Of First Language Towards Student’s Pronunciation This study investigates the phonological interference of the first language (L1) on the English pronunciation of Palopo students. The research aims to identify the types of phonological interference and the factors influencing students’ pronunciation when learning English as a foreign language. Using a descriptive qualitative design, data were collected through pronunciation tests, audio recordings, and interviews. The pronunciation data were analyzed using content and thematic analysis, referring to English phonetic standards from the Oxford Learner’s Pocket Dictionary. The findings revealed three major types of phonological interference: sound addition, sound omission, and sound replacement, with sound replacement being the most dominant type. Common replacement patterns included /ð/ → /d/, /θ/ → /t/, and /v/ → /p/, indicating systematic transfer from the L1 phonological system. The results further showed that L1 influence, lack of pronunciation practice, and low self-confidence were the main factors affecting pronunciation accuracy. title: Factors of Language Anxiety Affecting Self-Confidence in English Speaking Skills of EFL Undergraduate Students
text_snippet: Factors of Language Anxiety Affecting Self-Confidence in English Speaking Skills of EFL Undergraduate Students Speaking English fluently is crucial for both professional and personal development. However, language anxiety can be a problem for EFL learners because it serves as an emotional barrier that tends to undermine their confidence and prevent their development in speaking. To assist learners' confidence and success, it is vital to recognize the various factors that contribute to this concern. The various factors of language anxiety that affect undergraduate English education students’ self-confidence in speaking, especially students at Universitas Kristen Satya Wacana (UKSW) that come from Bengkayang, Kalimantan Barat are explored in this study. A quantitative research design is used and the researchers collected the data from 30 students using an adapted questionnaire from the Foreign Language Speaking Anxiety Scale to examine four anxiety dimensions: fear of negative evaluation, unpreparedness, public speaking fear and shyness, and general speaking class anxiety. The findings show that those four factors significantly influence students’ self-confidence though fear of negative evaluation emerged as the most crucial one. title: Linguistic Features of End-of-Chapter Interrogative Sentences in Lao Language Textbooks for Primary Education
text_snippet: Linguistic Features of End-of-Chapter Interrogative Sentences in Lao Language Textbooks for Primary Education This qualitative document analysis aims to analyze the linguistic features of end-of-chapter questions in the newly revised Lao language textbooks for primary education. The sample for analysis comprised 98 end-of-chapter questions selected through purposive sampling from the grade 3, grade 4, and grade 5 textbooks in Lao. The research instrument was a linguistic feature analysis form developed by the researchers based on Lao grammatical theory and linguistic principles, designed to classify word types (e.g., interrogative words, verbs, nouns, adjectives, adverbs) and sentence structures. The findings indicate that the linguistic features of the questions exhibit a systematic progression across grade levels. In Grade 3, the questions predominantly use foundational language, featuring concrete vocabulary and simple sentence structures to solicit basic information (“Nyang” (what), “Sai” (where), “Phai” (who), “Nyon Nyang” (why), “Naeo Dai” (how)). In grade 4, there is an initial introduction of abstract language and more formal imperative language. title: Learning Strategies in ESP of Vocational High School Students
text_snippet: Learning Strategies in ESP of Vocational High School Students This study aims to explore the English language learning strategies employed by nursing students at SMK Amanah Husada. A qualitative descriptive method was used in this research, with data collected through questionnaires and open-ended interviews. The data were analyzed using coding techniques to identify key emerging themes. The findings revealed that students employ various strategies in learning English for nursing. These strategies include listening to English songs, practicing singing English songs, speaking practice, engaging in dialogues, and role-playing, participating in study group discussions, watching movies, playing games, writing, watching YouTube videos, and using Google Translate as a learning aid. It can be concluded that students tend to use learning strategies that are easily accessible, enjoyable, and aligned with their daily habits.

title: The Effectiveness of Story Map to Teach Students’ Recount Text Writing
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Story Map to Teach Students’ Recount Text Writing This study aims to investigate whether the use of Story Map for eighth-grade students of SMPN 1 Sungai Raya affects students' writing ability in recount text or not. This study employed a pre- experimental design with a single group, consisting of both pre-test and post-test, as the research approach. The population of this study consisted of all eighth-grade students at SMPN 1 Sungai Raya, totaling 246 students. The sample was selected through cluster random sampling, and the result was a class of VIII B, consisting of 30 students. Data was obtained from the results of the pre-test and post-test and analyzed using the t-test and effect size formulas. The t-test result was 11.67. The t-test table, with degrees of freedom (df) = 29 and a significance level of 0.05, yielded a value of 2.045. These data indicate that the t-test is higher than the t-table (11.67 > 2.045). This shows that the null hypothesis (H0) is rejected and the alternative hypothesis (Ha) is accepted. The findings also revealed that the effect size score for the treatment was 2.01, categorized as a strong effect. title: Enhancing Career-Oriented English Skills Through Task-Based Writing and Speaking Activities: A Classroom-Based Reflection
text_snippet: Enhancing Career-Oriented English Skills Through Task-Based Writing and Speaking Activities: A Classroom-Based Reflection This study examines the implementation of Task Based Language Teaching (TBLT) with insights from the Genre-Based Approach (GBA) in the English 2 course at Politeknik Negeri Banjarmasin in order to engage students in authentic workplace communication tasks and develop career-oriented English skills. Carried out the reflective qualitative design through classroom-based self-study, the research involved 129 students from Information Systems, Digital Business, and Accounting Information Systems study programs. The writing tasks included opinion, report text, summary, guided curriculum vitae and cover letter writing, followed by job interview practice, designed based on students’ needs analysis. Data were collected through observation over twelve sessions and analysed through reflective and thematic interpretation. Findings indicate that writing tasks helped students’ express ideas, practice coherence, and apply a formal tone, while serving as preparation for oral tasks. The sequencing from writing to speaking supported skill progression, though challenges emerged. title: Research Formatting Dilemmas of College Students: Basis for Policy Formulation
text_snippet: Research Formatting Dilemmas of College Students: Basis for Policy Formulation Scientific research revolutionizes our modern life today, making it an integral aspect of curricula in higher education. As student-researchers generally have both positive and negative attitudes and experiences in doing research, it is a reality that following religious research formats may pose significant challenges. With those realities, the study identified the research formatting challenges faced by college students at a state university in the Philippines to inform the development of a research policy. It investigated the specific formatting difficulties and perceptions of college students on the importance of adhering to formatting guidelines. The study employed the descriptive qualitative design through semi-structured interviews. Fifteen (15) students who were study-leaders were purposively selected to participate in the interview process. The interview transcripts were treated using thematic analysis proposed by Clarke and Braun. The study suggested that a lack of formatting, codification, and the location of research storage resulted in inefficiencies in conducting research. title: Enhancing Students’ Speaking Ability through Role Play within the Communicative Language Teaching Framework
text_snippet: Enhancing Students’ Speaking Ability through Role Play within the Communicative Language Teaching Framework This study examines students' perceptions and challenges in using role-play within the framework of Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) to improve their English-speaking abilities. Employing a mixed-methods research design, the study involved 35 students from the Software Engineering (RPL) program at SMK YPKK 1 Sleman, Yogyakarta. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires using a four-point Likert scale. At the same time, qualitative insights were obtained from semi-structured interviews with three selected participants representing high, medium, and low performance categories. The questionnaire findings revealed that students' perceptions of role-play in CLT were generally positive, with an average score of 78, categorized as good. Students reported that role-play enhanced their confidence, fluency, and ability to communicate effectively in English. However, interview results identified several challenges. Internal factors included limited proficiency, lack of confidence, performance anxiety, and insufficient preparation, whereas external factors involved difficulties in understanding cue cards, limited vocabulary, and feelings of pressure when performing in front

title: The Effectiveness of KWL Strategy on Students' Reading Comprehension of Recount Text
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of KWL Strategy on Students' Reading Comprehension of Recount Text The research aims to find out the effectiveness of the KWL strategy on students' reading comprehension of recount text in the eighth-grade students of SMP Negeri 1 Sungai Raya in the Academic Year 2023/2024. This research was pre-experimental research with one group pre-test and post-test design. The population of this research was the eighth-grade students of SMP Negeri 1 Sungai Raya Academic Year 2023/2024. The total number of students was 224, and the research sample was class VIII B, which consisted of 30 students. The measurement technique was employed to collect data. The result of the t-test of the treatment was 16,36. The degree of freedom (df) = 29, significant at level 0.05, was 2.045. This data showed that the t-test was higher than the t-table (16,36 > 2.045). It indicated that the null hypothesis was rejected, and the alternative hypothesis (,which is the effectiveness of the KWL strategy on students' reading comprehension in recount text, was accepted. The findings showed significantly higher levels of students' reading comprehension during the implementation of the KWL strategy, demonstrating its effectiveness as an instructional strategy for reading comprehension.

title: Secondary school managers’ implementation of positive learner discipline: A Namibian legal framework
text_snippet: Secondary school managers’ implementation of positive learner discipline: A Namibian legal framework The management of the implementation of positive learner discipline is one of the crucial tasks that should be performed by school managers. Namibia is one of the countries in the world that abolished corporal punishment and introduced positive learner discipline. Namibian schools still face the challenge of learners with ill-disciplined behaviour. Even though these schools have learner discipline policies, they still experience the lack of discipline. Numerous Namibian scholars have conducted research on learner discipline in schools. However, these studies have not shown clear empirical evidence on how schools implement the legal framework that guides positive learner discipline. The aim of this study was to explore secondary school managers’ implementation of positive learner discipline within a Namibian legal framework. A qualitative research approach and an interpretative paradigm were used. The study was conducted in the Khomas Region of Namibia. Purposive sampling was used to sample eight secondary schools, whereby eight principals and eight Heads of Departments were selected as participants. title: The Use of Drama-Based Instruction to Enhance Students’ Narrative Writing Skills
text_snippet: The Use of Drama-Based Instruction to Enhance Students’ Narrative Writing Skills This study investigated the effectiveness of drama-based instruction in enhancing students’ English learning performance and explored students’ perceptions toward its implementation in an EFL classroom. The study was conducted at SMPN 5 Semarang involving 31 ninth-grade students. A quantitative research design with a one-group pretest–posttest approach was employed. The instruments used in this study included a narrative writing test administered as both pretest and posttest, as well as a questionnaire consisting of 25 items to measure students’ perceptions of drama-based instruction. The treatment was carried out over seven meetings, focusing on the application of drama activities integrated with narrative text writing. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential analysis through a paired samples t-test to examine the significance of students’ performance improvement. The findings revealed a noticeable increase in students’ posttest scores compared to their pretest scores, indicating that drama-based instruction positively affected students’ learning performance. title: Assessing ICT Integration in Ghanaian Primary Schools: Contextual Factors that Shape Practice in Developing Nations
text_snippet: Assessing ICT Integration in Ghanaian Primary Schools: Contextual Factors that Shape Practice in Developing Nations This research explores the extent of ICT integration in resource-limited elementary schools in Ghana and examines the contextual factors that influence its implementation. The study employed a convergent mixed-methods case study approach to gather both quantitative and qualitative data from 335 instructors through open-ended questions and structured questionnaires, complemented by in-depth interviews with ten teachers and education officials. The results suggest that, despite a high perceived utility (M = 4.45), ICT utilisation and teacher confidence remain relatively low (M = 1.28; M = 1.21). Problems such as inadequate infrastructure, limited opportunities for professional growth, and insufficient institutional support are the primary causes of this discrepancy. Qualitative findings also emphasise insufficient institutional support, inadequate professional development structures, and resource constraints as prominent obstacles. title: Tailoring Local Content into English for Tourism Materials: Needs of Tourism Students in Central Kalimantan
text_snippet: Tailoring Local Content into English for Tourism Materials: Needs of Tourism Students in Central Kalimantan English for Tourism in tourism education institutions should equip students with English skills relevant to their academic and workplace settings. In Central Kalimantan, the tourism students must also have the knowledge of local tourism. Unfortunately, no English for Tourism book currently includes relevant local content. To address this gap, a needs analysis was conducted to explore the necessary language skills, topics, and local content to be incorporated into English for Tourism materials for these students. This research employed both quantitative and qualitative methods, utilizing a questionnaire and a focused-group interview. This research has shown a number of findings. It was revealed that the students prioritize speaking, listening and vocabulary, followed by other skills and components. They also need the materials that cover a range of topics, including general and local tourism content. Tour guiding, describing tourist spots, and tourism-related jobs were among the preferred essential topics. title: Tracing the Past: Exploring the Link Between Past Tense Mastery and Students’ Written in EFL Learners
text_snippet: Tracing the Past: Exploring the Link Between Past Tense Mastery and Students’ Written in EFL Learners This study aims to explore the relationship between students’ mastery of past tense and their ability to write about past experiences. A total of 40 eleventh-grade students participated in the research. Data were collected through two written assessments: a grammar test focusing on past tense usage and a writing task that required students to retell a story using appropriate tenses. The grammar test included multiple-choice questions and sentence transformation items, while the writing task offered four topics from which students chose one. The results of the grammar test revealed a mean score of 4.3, which falls into the “Poor” category. This indicates that students generally struggle with understanding and applying past tense forms correctly. On the other hand, the writing assessment showed a mean score of 6.9, classified as “Fairly Good.” This suggests that, despite limited grammar mastery, students were moderately successful in expressing ideas about past events in written form. To determine the strength of the correlation between the two variables, the Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient was applied. title: Assessment of the Benefits and Challenges of Digital Braille Assistive Devices in Promoting Inclusivity of Learners with Visual Impairment in Kenya
text_snippet: Assessment of the Benefits and Challenges of Digital Braille Assistive Devices in Promoting Inclusivity of Learners with Visual Impairment in Kenya This study focuses on assessment of the benefits and challenges of digital braille assistive devices in relation to their relevance in promoting inclusivity of learners with visual impairment (VI) in special and integrated education. The study was guided by universal design for learning and assistive technology theories. The study adopted a descriptive survey design within a mixed methodology approach. The study was restricted within 2 institutions in Kenya: a private University (mainstream) and a special school for the blind. The two key study objectives were to assess the benefits of digital assistive devices for the learners with VI in relation to promoting inclusivity in education. Secondly, the study examined the challenges learners face in using these devices in special and mainstream education. The findings show that using digital braille assistive devices for visually impaired learners offer significant benefits. The key benefits include promoting educational access, learner’s independence and enhancing learning opportunities. However, several barriers remain inadequately addressed. title: Student Difficulties in Achieving Effective English Learning Skills
text_snippet: Student Difficulties in Achieving Effective English Learning Skills This study aims to describe the learning difficulties of Yogyakarta Administrative Management Academy students in acquiring English language skills. The survey targeted 205 students enrolled in the even semester of the 2023-2024 academic year. Qualitative description was used in data analysis. From the results of this study, two factors of difficulty were found, namely internal and external. The causes of students' learning difficulties from internal factors such as low level of intelligence, low aptitude in English subjects, lack of interest in learning, and low motivation to learn. Students attend only out of obligation and to get good grades and complete assignments, not to learn English as an international language that is so important today. The external factors that affect students who have difficulty learning English include a lack of support for the use of English at home or in the community, as well as limited opportunities to use English outside the classroom. title: Gender Representation in Madurese Folktales: A Critical Discourse Analysis
text_snippet: Gender Representation in Madurese Folktales: A Critical Discourse Analysis This study explores gender representation in Madurese folktales using Norman Fairclough's Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA). By analyzing two selected folktales, The Origin of the Madurese People and Menak Sanaya, the research examines textual, discursive, and sociocultural dimensions to understand how gender roles are portrayed and their implications on societal perceptions. The findings reveal a recurring pattern of patriarchal ideologies where male characters are depicted as dominant, protective, and decision-makers. In contrast, female characters are relegated to subordinate roles, often portrayed as passive and reliant on male intervention. These representations reflect traditional Madurese societal values and contribute to the reinforcement of gender hierarchies. The study highlights how narratives serve as tools for intergenerational transmission of cultural norms, shaping collective consciousness and perpetuating gender stereotypes. Insights from this research emphasize the need for critical engagement with cultural narratives to foster discussions on gender equality.

title: English Students’ Perceptions Towards The Implementation Of Online Learning During Covid-19 Pandemic
text_snippet: English Students’ Perceptions Towards The Implementation Of Online Learning During Covid-19 Pandemic The aim of this study is to achieve one objective. It is to describe the students’ perception toward the implementation of online learning during Covid-19 pandemic. To achieve this objective, a descriptive survey was implemented. It used the theory of descriptive survey by Creswell (2018). The data collected through a questionnaire and the results were presented in percentage. Furthermore, the subject in this researcher was students in Language Education Study Program in Teacher Training and Education Faculty in Universitas Tanjungpura academic year 2022/2023 of batch 2018 until 2021 regular A and PPAPK which consisted of 322 students. The process of data analysis was started by determining the ideal score and the level of student’s perception by percentage formula. As a result, the point of conclusion is concluded. The students’ perception of the implementation of online learning during Covid-19 pandemic was positive perception (70%) and it’s indicated as a high percentage of positive perception. The positive perception includes the effective class management, infrastructure learning absorption, learning activity and improvement of student's accomplishment.

title: The Correlation among Reading Motivation, Reading Anxiety, and Reading Comprehension of Tenth-Grade Students in Palembang
text_snippet: The Correlation among Reading Motivation, Reading Anxiety, and Reading Comprehension of Tenth-Grade Students in Palembang This study examined the correlation among reading motivation, reading anxiety, and reading comprehension of tenth-grade students in Palembang. A quantitative correlational research design was employed, involving 509 students from SMA Bina Warga 1 Palembang and SMA Negeri 15 Palembang. Using cluster random sampling, 107 students were selected as the sample. Data were collected through a reading comprehension test and two questionnaires measuring reading motivation and reading anxiety. The findings indicated no significant correlation between reading motivation and reading comprehension (r = 0.087, p = 0.375), indicating that motivation to read did not influence students’ understanding of texts. Likewise, no notable correlation was identified between reading anxiety and reading comprehension (r = -0.022, p = 0.824), suggesting that anxiety was not a determining factor. These results revealed that reading motivation and reading anxiety did not have a substantial effect on reading comprehension. title: Adapting to the New Frontier The Transformative Role of Academics in Shaping Higher Education
text_snippet: Adapting to the New Frontier The Transformative Role of Academics in Shaping Higher Education The higher education trajectory has transformed significantly since 2020, largely due to the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. This period saw both students and academics navigating personal and professional transitions, leading to mental health and work-life balance challenges. Education 5.0, characterized by extensive use of technology, calls for a reassessment of current teaching practices and an exploration of the evolving role of academics in the post-2025 higher education space. Academics are crucial in driving research, designing curricula, and mentoring students. This study is grounded in Gagne’s Conditions of Learning Theory, the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) model, and Technological-Motivational-Learning Theory. The focus is on envisioning how the academic landscape should adapt to meet the needs of Generation Alpha, who will enter higher education in 2029. There is a need to nurture intellectual curiosity, inspire critical thinking, and prepare students for future challenges. title: Rethinking Teacher Professional Development in Public Secondary Schools in Zimbabwe
text_snippet: Rethinking Teacher Professional Development in Public Secondary Schools in Zimbabwe Effective professional development practices are instrumental to the performance of schools as teachers play a pivotal role in shaping educational outcomes for learners in any country. In Zimbabwe, economic and social challenges have affected the availability, relevance, and effectiveness of professional development for teachers in public secondary schools. The principals' lack of instructional leadership and poor management skills have exacerbated the situation. Major gaps exist between current practices and strategic goals, highlighting the need for improved professional development. The study is motivated by the urgent need to rethink and redefine professional development in schools in Zimbabwe to improve teacher performance and retention. Situated in the interpretivism paradigm, this qualitative study used semi-structured interviews and document study to gather data. Findings highlight the urgent need for context-specific, continuous, and culturally responsive professional development programmes that address classroom management, discipline, and indigenous knowledge systems. title: English Language Learning Experiences in Selecting Youtube Video
text_snippet: English Language Learning Experiences in Selecting Youtube Video YouTube can be a valuable tool for enhancing students' understanding of the English language, as it is well-recognized as a website that offers a diverse range of videos across many contexts. YouTube is a valuable and accessible resource for learning English due to its wide collection of instructional videos (Khoiroh, 2021). This research aims to determine the criteria for selecting YouTube videos, the challenges, and the impact of using YouTube videos to learn speaking and listening skills through descriptive qualitative research. The participants of this research are four students from class A+ sixth-semester English education regular-A students at Universitas Tanjungpura in the 2023/2024 academic year.
